title: 2002 AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: Mr. Earl E. Bird leaves his house for work at exactly \(8{:}00\) A.M. every morning. When he averages \(40\) miles per hour, he arrives at his workplace three minutes late. When he averages \(60\) miles per hour, he arrives three minutes early. At what average speed, in miles per hour, should Mr. Bird drive to arrive at his workplace precisely on time?

solutions.text:
Let \(t\) be the time in hours to arrive on time. Since three minutes is \(0.05\) hours, \(40(t+0.05) = 60(t-0.05).\)

This gives \(40t + 2 = 60t - 3,\) so \(t = 0.25.\) The distance is \(40(0.25+0.05) = 12\) miles, and the required speed is \(\dfrac{12}{0.25} = 48\) miles per hour.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(t\) be the on-time travel time in hours; three minutes is \(0.05\) hours
Set \(40(t+0.05) = 60(t-0.05),\) solve for \(t,\) then find the distance
